title: The measure feed, the alert delivery path and the run record have no target artifact once the data lake and the job monitor are removed
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-030 sections 3, 4, 12, 13 and 14; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4 (JOB-06, JOB-15); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 10 and 42; _work/msr/context/P3.md
section: s4 Flow steps 6, 9, 11; s10 Authority; s12.3 Events published; s14 Validation and messages
description: Four surfaces of the legacy story are gone in the target and no source names their replacement. (a) JOB-15 copied the queue_measure snapshot to the data lake for Power BI nightly; DP-17 removes the lake and the INT-19 and INT-20 batch, and no source states how rwb-reporting receives the queue, ageing and breach measures, or on which fields it projects them. (b) MSG-P3-028, MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-029 were delivered by the monolith's notification path and the story assigns no contract for a notice service, so the delivery path (ACE notification path or rwb-comms) is unnamed. (c) The legacy job monitor held the run record and listed a case that stayed with MSG-P7-003; with the Quartz job retired the run record is the workflow record, and no source gives its shape or a read for it. (d) The rerun call POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun under Platform administration U has no operation in the ownership map and no stated operator surface.
evidence: RWB-E1-030 section 4 step 9 (JOB-15 copies the snapshot to the data lake), section 12 (job table: events published, idempotency key, restart from the job monitor; the rerun endpoint under P1), section 14 (the three messages); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 rows JOB-06 and JOB-15; Architecture v5 slide 8 'Data lake / Power BI not connected (INT-19/20 removed)' and slide 10 for the notification path; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 row and R4 topic naming; context pack P3 lists 22 REST operations, none of them a jobs rerun or a run record.
proposed: Name the reporting feed and its fields (events only, or a published measure read) in the P9 contract before wave 1 closes, name the delivery service for the three messages, and state whether the run record and the rerun surface are a workflow read plus a Schedule trigger or a published operation, then add the agreed rows to the ownership map.

title: The published run record and the rerun operation of the legacy contract have no target shape
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-030 section 12 (job table, GET /api/recovery/v1/cases, POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun); _work/msr/context/P3.md ownership rows; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42
section: s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.6 Schedules; s7 AC5
description: The legacy contract published three things this baseline cannot copy: the job table of JOB-06 with its restart and idempotency statements, the rerun endpoint under Platform administration U with 409 when the job is running, and the in-process QueueMeasureService interface read by P9. The ownership map gives only three read operations for the case side and no rerun, and the interface's consumer disappears with the data lake, so the contract has to state what a consumer can read for a business date (the moves through GET /cases and the snapshot through GET /queues) and that the run record is the workflow record. No source fixes the field list of a published run record or the status codes of a rerun call, so both are left out of the document and raised here.
evidence: RWB-E1-030 section 12: the job table (trigger, job name, schedule, input, output, events published, idempotency key, restart) and 'POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (P1) for JOB-06: Platform administration U; 409 when the job is running'; context pack P3 REST rows (22 operations, no jobs and no run record); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 row.
proposed: State in the P3 contract baseline review whether a business date's run is readable as a document resource; if it is, add the operation and the ownership row, and publish the run record schema in version 1 of RWB-P3-E1030-CON before the reporting consumer builds against it.

title: No source gives the operating values for the rebalance Schedule or the deployment
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-030 sections 4 and 13; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4 (JOB-06 daily 06:30); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 44; _work/msr/context/P3.md
section: s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s12.6 Schedules; s17 Guardrails
description: The chart and the Schedule need values that no source provides: the business time zone of the 06:30 firing, the catch-up window and overlap policy of the Schedule, the replica counts, resource limits and ingress host of the two deployments, the threshold and window of the held-snapshot alert and of the missing-run alert, the dead-letter rate and depth bands, and the retry values of the two activities. The legacy story gives only the 06:30 time and the feature flag name; the batch design gives the same time and no zone; the architecture slides give the schedule pattern but no operational number. Because the story must not invent a value, every one of them is a value in the values file with no default chosen here.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-06 (Daily 06:30); RWB-E1-030 sections 4 and 13 (`rwb.p3.rebalance`); Architecture v5 slide 44 (stuck workflow scan every 5 min, alert) and slide 8 (namespace and task queue only); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 row.
proposed: Set the values in the rwb-case values files per environment, confirm the zone and the catch-up window with the business owner and the platform team at the SIT dry run, and record the agreed values in the runbook section each alert links.
